clue.text: Oven with glowing exterior got very hot

indicators.note: the glowing word forms the outside layer, wrapped round the oven word

parts.note: something glowing is red-hot, so red
an oast is a kiln for drying hops

explanation.surface: A cook notices the oven's outside glowing and finds things very hot indeed.
explanation.walkthrough: An oast is the kiln used in Kent for drying hops.
explanation.definitionFit: To be roasted is to have been subjected to intense heat, as in a sweltering room.

clue.text: Second fight perhaps upset more gentle children

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the word upside down, so read from the bottom

parts.note: tamer means more gentle, less wild

explanation.surface: A rematch upsets gentler children.
explanation.definitionFit: A rematch is a second contest between the same opponents, a boxing bout perhaps.

clue.text: Marine life trapped by undersea glaciers rising

indicators.note: rising says the hidden letters are read backwards
the letters are held inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Sea organisms caught beneath glaciers rise to the surface.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft put 'trapped' in the definition; 'trapped by' is the signal that the letters lie inside 'undersea glaciers', so the definition is 'Marine life' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Algae include seaweeds and plankton, forms of marine plant life.

clue.text: Sticky little growths twist leg out of shape

indicators.note: the letters are bent into a different form

explanation.surface: Twist a leg out of shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sticky' plays on stick: small twigs are little sticks. Twiglets are also a British stick-shaped savoury snack.
explanation.definitionFit: Twiglets are small twigs, the little stick-like shoots growing from branches.

clue.text: University dons brought up poor artist's feeble effort

indicators.note: to don is to put on, so the reversed word wears the university letter inside it
in a down clue the word is read upwards, so reversed

parts.note: bad means poor in quality

explanation.surface: University lecturers raised a weak artist's bad attempt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dons' looks like university teachers; it is the verb to put on.
explanation.definitionFit: A daub is a crude, unskilful painting, a bad artist's effort.

clue.text: Aquatic animal's tail appearing first in spring

indicators.note: the final letter of the sea creature is shifted to the front of the word

parts.note: a manatee is a sea cow, a large aquatic mammal

explanation.surface: A naturalist notes a sea creature's tail emerging first in springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' looks like the season; it is the verb, as in to spring from a source.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to issue or originate from a source.

clue.text: Staring angrily at first person shouting on the phone

indicators.note: heard over the phone, so the words are taken by their sound

parts.note: I is the first person, bawling is shouting

explanation.surface: Someone glares at the first person who yells down the phone.
explanation.definitionFit: To eyeball someone is to stare at them hard, often confrontationally.

clue.text: Knowing when student fails to finish

parts.note: as means when, as in as I left

indicators.note: the student word loses its last letter

parts.note: a tutee is a student taught by a tutor

explanation.surface: A shrewd observation when a pupil drops out before completion.
explanation.definitionFit: Astute means shrewd and perceptive, hence knowing.

clue.text: Transmuting metal is primarily his concern

definitions.text: Transmuting metal is primarily his concern

indicators.note: changing form, so the letters are converted into a new arrangement
takes the first letters of his and concern

explanation.surface: Turning base metal into gold is chiefly his business.
explanation.definitionFit: An alchemist sought to transmute base metals into gold, his whole concern.

clue.text: Concentrate less, getting left out, hence missing opening

indicators.note: the letter for left is removed from less
hence loses its first letter

explanation.surface: Focus less on being excluded, and so avoid missing the start.
explanation.walkthrough: L is the usual abbreviation for left.
explanation.definitionFit: An essence is a concentrated extract, as in vanilla essence.

clue.text: Importance publication attached to naked figure full of sex appeal

parts.note: a mag is a magazine, a publication

indicators.note: the naked figure word holds the sex appeal word within it

parts.note: a nude is a naked figure in art
it is old slang for sex appeal, as in the It girl

explanation.surface: A glossy magazine attaches great importance to a sexy nude.
explanation.walkthrough: IT for sex appeal comes from the 1920s 'It girl' Clara Bow.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnitude is greatness of size or significance, hence importance.

clue.text: Fare from Mexico via America included in high cost

indicators.note: the America letter is placed inside the rearranged word
high as in intoxicated, so the letters of cost are jumbled

explanation.surface: Mexican food imported via America comes at a high cost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high' looks like part of 'high cost'; it is the anagram signal on 'cost', giving TCOS, with A put inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacos are folded tortillas with fillings, a staple Mexican dish.

clue.text: High-pitched sound starts to bother ladies aboard plane?

indicators.note: the initials go inside the tree word, as passengers go aboard

parts.note: a plane is a kind of tree, the plane tree

indicators.note: takes the first letters of bother and ladies

explanation.surface: A high-pitched noise from the start bothers the women on board an aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plane?' looks like an aircraft; the question mark flags the plane tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Treble is the highest vocal or instrumental register, a high-pitched sound.

clue.text: Criticise article about the great and the good

parts.note: to pan is to criticise harshly
the is the definite article
on means about, as in a book on birds

explanation.surface: A columnist slates a piece on the great and the good.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantheon is the set of most revered figures in a field, its great and good.

clue.text: Surprising French article about warning received by new witness

indicators.note: the warning sits on top of the witness and new letters that take it in, in this down clue

parts.note: un is the French indefinite article
fore is the golfer's warning shout
to see is to witness

explanation.surface: A French news item about a warning given to a fresh witness.
explanation.walkthrough: FORE is shouted on a golf course to warn players of an incoming ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unforeseen was not expected, so it comes as a surprise.

clue.text: They start to lead saint astray without conviction

indicators.note: the letters wander off course into a new order
takes the first letter of lead

explanation.surface: People begin to lead a holy man off the right path, but half-heartedly.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something without conviction is doing it with hesitation and uncertainty.

clue.text: Letters providing protection for owner of mobile home?

definitions.meaning: correspondence sent by the ordinary post

definitions.text: protection for owner of mobile home?
definitions.meaning: armour, as in chain mail, for the creature that carries its shell as a home

explanation.surface: Letters that safeguard someone living in a caravan.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'mobile home' is a snail's shell; mail is armour.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a jokey name for slow conventional post, as opposed to email.

clue.text: Divers may use this spear hunting fish

definitions.meaning: a jackknife position with straight legs used in springboard diving
a long pole weapon carried by foot soldiers
a predatory freshwater fish that hunts other fish

explanation.surface: Scuba divers might use a spear when hunting for fish.
explanation.walkthrough: Three meanings: a diving position, an infantry weapon, and a predatory fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The diving position, the old infantry weapon and the predatory fish all share this name.

clue.text: Auditor's most appropriate passion for another auditor?

indicators.note: an auditor is a listener, so the words are taken as heard

parts.note: very means most appropriate, as in the very thing, and fire is passion

explanation.surface: An accountant's ideal enthusiasm for a fellow accountant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auditor' appears twice: first a listener, then a checker of accounts.
explanation.definitionFit: An auditor checks accounts for accuracy, which is what a verifier does.

clue.text: Support visit to delay postponement of legal proceedings

definitions.meaning: to remain somewhere as a guest

explanation.surface: A lawyer backs a visit made to stall a court adjournment.
explanation.walkthrough: Four separate meanings strung together.
explanation.definitionFit: Each sense is standard: a prop, a sojourn, a check, and a court-ordered suspension.

clue.text: Ration in the army?

definitions.meaning: a portion of food given out
on active duty as an enlisted soldier

explanation.definitionFit: A serving is a helping of food, and soldiers are said to be serving.

clue.text: Opiate isn't derived from this plant

indicators.note: the plant name is made out of the letters of these words rearranged

explanation.surface: A botanical note: no opiate is extracted from this plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The poinsettia is a Mexican plant with red bracts, popular at Christmas.

clue.text: Agents gripped by first half of writer's supplement

indicators.note: the agents word is held inside the halved writer word
keeps the opening three of the writer word's six letters

parts.note: an author is a writer
G-men are FBI agents

explanation.surface: Spies are held by part of an author's appendix.
explanation.walkthrough: G-men is American slang for FBI agents (Government men).
explanation.definitionFit: To augment is to add to or increase, as a supplement does.

clue.text: Introduce character providing opening for somewhat lifeless hosts

indicators.note: the lifeless word holds the single letter inside, like a host with a guest

parts.note: inert means lifeless, without motion

indicators.note: the letter that begins somewhat

explanation.surface: A new character livens up a dull host.
explanation.definitionFit: To insert something is to put it in, to introduce it.

clue.text: Weakened and let guards empty latrine

indicators.note: the let word surrounds the emptied latrine word, as a guard encloses

parts.note: to let a property is to have rented it out

indicators.note: the latrine word with its inside removed leaves its outer letters

explanation.surface: Someone gave in and allowed guards to clean out the latrine.
explanation.definitionFit: To have relented is to have softened or yielded, so weakened in resolve.

clue.text: Defect after leader's been taken ill

indicators.note: the first letter is removed from the defect word

parts.note: a failing is a defect or weakness

explanation.surface: A defector reports that the party leader has fallen ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Defect' looks like the verb to change sides; it is the noun, a shortcoming.
explanation.definitionFit: Ailing means unwell, in poor health.

clue.text: Duckweed reportedly forming large area across the pond

indicators.note: the words are taken by how they sound when spoken

parts.note: an eider is a sea duck and to hoe is to weed

explanation.surface: Pond weed is said to be forming a large mat across the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duckweed' is split: duck gives EIDER, weed gives HOE. 'across the pond' means in America.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is a large US state, across the Atlantic from Britain.

clue.text: Form of insect life in Papua New Guinea finally disappearing

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh arrangement of the letters
the chosen letter is removed from Papua
takes the last letter of Guinea

explanation.surface: An insect species from Papua New Guinea is finally dying out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes A from Guinea, 'disappearing' removes it from PAPUA leaving PPUA, and 'New' rearranges that.
explanation.definitionFit: The pupa is the chrysalis stage between larva and adult insect.

clue.text: Interim agenda includes public perception of company

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words interim agenda, run together

explanation.surface: A board's interim agenda includes the firm's public reputation.
explanation.definitionFit: A company's image is the impression the public holds of it.

clue.text: Illustrate Greek mathematician moving his line, reflecting his character

indicators.note: one letter of the mathematician's name shifts to a new place in it

parts.note: Euclid was the Greek author of the Elements
L is an abbreviation for line

indicators.note: the Greek letter is read backwards, as in a mirror

parts.note: eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: An ancient geometer redraws his line, revealing his true nature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' shifts the L in EUCLID to make ELUCID; 'reflecting' turns ETA into ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To elucidate is to make clear or explain, as an illustration does.

clue.text: Setter's cheering when cycling

definitions.note: read as setter is; a setting agent that makes jellies firm

indicators.note: the last letter goes round to the front of the word

parts.note: elating means cheering, raising spirits

explanation.surface: The crossword compiler is cheerful when out on a bike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' looks like the compiler; it is something that sets jelly.
explanation.definitionFit: Gelatin is the protein used to make jellies and desserts set firm.

clue.text: Set of terminals connects display to computer socket

parts.note: to air something is to display it publicly
a port is a connection socket on a computer

explanation.surface: A technician connects a display to a computer port, wiring up the terminals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terminals' suggests computing; here they are passenger buildings.
explanation.definitionFit: An airport typically comprises several passenger terminals.
